question:
**Case Study: Societal Data in Psychology—Symmetric, Skew-Symmetric Matrix Applications**

A psychologist records mutual trust scores (scale 0–10) between individuals A, B, and C in a group, stored in a matrix $T$, where $t_{ij}$ is A's trust in B (etc.):

$T=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 6 & 8 \\ 5 & 0 & 4 \\ 3 & 7 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$

(a) Find the symmetric and skew-symmetric parts of $T$.

(b) Interpret the meaning of the skew-symmetric part in social science terms.

(c) Suggest what changing the matrix to be purely symmetric or skew-symmetric would mathematically and psychologically signify for the group.
explanation:
(a)

$T' = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 5 & 3 \\ 6 & 0 & 7 \\ 8 & 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

Symmetric: $S=\frac{1}{2}(T+T')=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 5.5 & 5.5 \\ 5.5 & 0 & 5.5 \\ 5.5 & 5.5 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

Skew-symmetric: $K=\frac{1}{2}(T-T')=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0.5 & 2.5 \\ -0.5 & 0 & -1.5 \\ -2.5 & 1.5 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

(b)

Skew-symmetric part represents asymmetry in trust relationships: e.g., if $a_{12}>a_{21}$, A trusts B more than B trusts A. These differences indicate directionality or imbalance in social ties.

(c)

If trust matrix is symmetric, all trust is mutual; if purely skew-symmetric, trust is perfectly anti-symmetric (if A trusts B, B distrusts A equally)—an unlikely situation. In psychological terms, a symmetric matrix models ideal mutual relationships, while a non-symmetric one exposes actual (potentially one-sided) dynamics.

options.A:
(a) $S=\frac12(T+T')=\begin{bmatrix}0&5.5&5.5\\5.5&0&5.5\\5.5&5.5&0\end{bmatrix}$ and $K=\frac12(T-T')=\begin{bmatrix}0&0.5&2.5\\-0.5&0&-1.5\\-2.5&1.5&0\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) $K$ measures imbalance or directionality in trust.
(c) A symmetric matrix means mutual trust; a purely skew-symmetric matrix represents perfectly anti-symmetric one-sided trust differences.
options.B:
(a) $S=T$ and $K=0$.
(b) There is no asymmetry in trust.
(c) The group already has perfectly mutual trust.
options.C:
(a) $S=0$ and $K=T$.
(b) All trust values are anti-symmetric.
(c) Symmetry has no psychological meaning.
options.D:
(a) $S=T'$ and $K=T+T'$.
(b) $K$ gives the total mutual trust.
(c) A skew-symmetric matrix means everyone trusts everyone equally.
